subject: Attribution runbook + per-route economics card request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@greenoptics.com>, GreenOptics Ops <ops@greenoptics.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Attribution runbook + per-route economics card request

Team —

GreenOptics reported a persistent spike last week where their tenant-level bill doubled for an hour. Support forwarded telemetry (attached) and asked for a clearer way to explain "who/what" caused the cost spike. 

Ask: can we ship a small, opinionated console card for per-route attribution that: 
- shows 3 lenses: token-cost breakdown (model/batches), tail-latency distribution, and top contributing request signatures (prompt hash / route id)
- surfaces a short, shareable attribution summary sentence and a link to an "Attribution runbook" with triage steps (what to check first, key queries, when to escalate to infra)

Constraints: GreenOptics is on Dedicated US-west with prefix caching enabled; they care about both cost and SLA exposure. We should aim for a design that can be wired into existing telemetry (traces + token billing table) without heavy infra changes.

Priority: P1 for observability roadmap (affects renewals if we can't give customers an actionable explanation). Proposed minimal delivery: mockup + data contract + runbook doc in two weeks.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Diego: confirm which telemetry fields we'll need (and whether we can get them from the current ingest)
2) Dylan: can you scope a small UX card (png mock) and the console hook to display attribution text + link to runbook?
3) Grace: please capture SLO/alerting implications for including the card in tenant dashboards.

I've attached the spike log GreenOptics sent and a quick CSV with candidate attribution keys. Sanjay — feel free to add context or correct anything.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior PM, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@greenoptics.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Attribution runbook + per-route economics card request

On Wed, Nov 15, 2028 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> GreenOptics reported a persistent spike last week where their tenant-level bill doubled for an hour. ...

Thanks for the clear ask — happy to lead the data contract. Quick notes from infra perspective: 

What I need from ingest / storage: 
- per-request: route_id, model, quantization_flag, token_in, token_out, batch_size, worker_pool_id
- per-tenant: prefix_cache_hit_rate (5m rollup), active_connections, pinned_model_variant
- trace ids for top N slow requests (so we can map latency -> request signature)

Feasibility: we already capture token-level billing and traces, but the missing piece is a compact request signature (normalized prompt hash) and an aggregation key for "route decomposition". I can add a short MapReduce job to synthesize a hourly attribution table but it will take ~6 dev-days and an infra change window (config rollout) to expose as a read API. If we limit the initial card to a 1-hour lookback and top-5 contributors we can avoid a full reindex.

Privacy note: ensure prompt-hash is irreversible for customers who require prompt privacy — we should surface counts and shapes, not raw prompts.

I'll add a PR with a proposed schema to OBS-7123 (link in thread).

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Infra
Redwood Inference

Attachment: attribution-matrix-v1.csv (preview)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@greenoptics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Attribution runbook + per-route economics card request

+1 on Diego's plan. From UX/console side here's a pragmatic rollout proposal: 

Phase 1 (2 weeks):
- Deliver a compact card (right rail) that shows: total cost delta (1h), pie by model, top-3 request hashes with % cost, and a one-line attribution sentence (auto-generated template). PNG mock attached (per-route-econ-card-v1.png).
- Card links to a hosted runbook doc (can be an internal markdown page) and the raw CSV download.

Phase 2 (4-6 weeks):
- Add interactive drilldown (time slider, trace links to AP, and latency histogram).
- Add a button to "open support ticket" prefilled with snapshot.

Questions / decisions needed: 
- Data latency tolerance: Diego, can the hourly attribution table be computed within 10 minutes of event completion? If not we should call out "data freshness" on the card.
- Escalation flow: Grace, what criteria should auto-populate the runbook's "escalate to infra" step? (e.g., cost delta >x% and tail-latency >y ms).

I'll slot designer time to iterate the mock if we confirm data fields.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Product Designer, Console
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@greenoptics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Attribution runbook + per-route economics card request

Marissa / team —

Thanks for jumping on this. The attached spike log is what our on-call sent; the CSV highlights the top noisy prompts we saw. Two asks from our side: 
1) Can GreenOptics be part of the beta for the initial card? We want to validate the attribution sentence and the exportable CSV.
2) We have a renewal meeting in mid-December; if you can provide a timeline and a one-slide summary we can show the CISO.

We care about prompt privacy — Diego's hash approach sounds fine as long as we can get human-readable context in the support export when approved by our security team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sanjay Kapoor
Director, Platform Ops
GreenOptics
